ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows trapezoid CDFG, the upper base CD is labeled 46; in the middle there is a line segment HE parallel to the upper and lower bases, labeled 38; the lower base GF is not directly given a length. Point H is on the left leg CG, and point E is on the right leg DF. Reasoning: The problem states that HE is the midline of trapezoid CDFG, so HE = (CD + GF) / 2. Substituting 38 = (46 + GF) / 2 gives 76 = 46 + GF, therefore GF = 30. Also because YZ is the midline of the smaller trapezoid HEFG, its two bases are HE = 38 and GF = 30, so YZ = (38 + 30) / 2 = 34.

Then use the text statement that YZ is the median of the smaller trapezoid HEFG. Its bases are HE = 38 and GF = 30, so YZ = (38 + 30)/2 = 34.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply the trapezoid median theorem: the median length equals the average of the two bases.
